extracted.intended_audience: students and writers of fiction; literary critics and close readers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for understanding, evaluating, and composing novels with attention to prophetic fiction, pattern, and rhythm; emphasizes aesthetic qualities (voice, unity, pattern) and trade-offs an author makes to achieve them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of prophetic fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Prophetic fiction has definite characteristics: it demands humility and the absence of the sense of humour; it reaches back (not necessarily to pity and love); it is spasmodically realistic; and it gives the sensation of a song or of sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Dostoevsky, Melville, D. H. Lawrence, Emily Brontë. Prophetic fiction differs from fantasy (which glances about and whose confusion is fundamental) because the prophet's face is towards unity and his confusion is incidental. The prophet is in a remoter emotional state while composing and tends to produce 'song' rather than 'talk.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Humility and suspension of humour in the prophetic mode
rubrics_metrics.description: To write or appreciate prophetic fiction one must adopt humility and suspend the sense of humour; readers are asked not to snigger or treat tragic elements lightly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author warns that prophetic works ask readers to lay aside their usual critical tools and humility is an aesthetic requirement. This is both a creator-side constraint and a reader expectation; failing to observe it risks losing the work's intended effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophetic voice: song over talk; non-reflective stance
rubrics_metrics.description: A prophet does not reflect or 'hammer away'; his writing is more like song (evocative, musical) than argumentative talk or sustained analytic reflection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contra Joyce: though Joyce has prophetic qualities, his 'workmanlike' undermining and talky deliberation disqualify him as a pure prophet. The prophetic voice is remote, irradiating, and focused on re-creation and evocation rather than logical exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermittent realism and foreground detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Prophetic novelists often exhibit intermittent realism: intense, patient accuracy about small foreground things (trials, staircases, products of a whale, fields of grass) that suddenly illuminate the scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small, well-observed particulars ('little things in the foreground') can make objects more vivid than ordinary domestic description. This beam-of-light manipulation renders familiar objects extraordinary; use sparingly and strategically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roughness of surface as positive aesthetic quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Great prophetic works often have a 'roughness of surface'—while passing before us they show dents, grooves, lumps and spikes that provoke immediate reactions; after the experience the roughness is forgotten and the work seems smooth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roughness (irregularities, abruptness) can be provocative and part of the work's power. Do not smooth away all asperities in pursuit of polish; the later sense of unity may absorb earlier roughness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reductive symbolism that silences the book
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not turn striking objects (e.g., the Delight ship or Queequeg's coffin in Moby Dick) into neat symbols, because even if the symbolism is correct it 'silences' the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow resonances and unformulated connections to exist; over-explicit symbolic reading can harmonize incidents and lose the rough richness and the song-like quality of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow an undercurrent or non-verbal theme (song/contest) to exist outside plot words
rubrics_metrics.description: Some novels carry a spiritual theme or undercurrent that 'lies outside words' and flows athwart action and surface morality (e.g., Moby Dick's contest and song).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize when a work's essential quality is an undercurrent rather than a statement; analysis that reduces the book to plot-level oppositions (good vs evil) may miss the prophetic song. Respect ambiguity and non-explicable elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depiction of evil as broad, impersonal, and personified beyond petty villainy
rubrics_metrics.description: Evil in great fiction can be envisaged without being merely social or sexual misconduct; it can be a transcendent, impersonal force rather than a conventional villain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast petty or conventional villains (who serve plots) with characters like Claggart or Melville's large-scale apprehension of evil. To depict real villainy, avoid merely giving the author an exploitable antagonist—aim for a more elemental, extraordinary conception of evil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern as an aesthetic, book-wide unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Pattern is an esthetic aspect by which a reader sees the book as a whole; it is most often nourished by the plot and causes us to perceive a structural shape (e.g., hour-glass, grand chain) even if we would not literally picture it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pattern appeals to the aesthetic sense (pleasure without knowing why) and often emerges from the plot's arrangement; it may be best expressed through pictorial similes but should be felt rather than taken literally. Pattern ties story, plot and characters into a coherent whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of pattern to author's mood and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: A pattern must be appropriate to the author's mood; a successful pattern harmonizes with atmosphere and the emotional coloration the author seeks to produce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Roman Pictures' grand chain suits its comic, sub-acid atmosphere; pattern is good only when it arises naturally from the author's sensibility. Choosing or forcing an unsuitable pattern reduces effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern is primarily drawn from plot; plot supplies nourishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Pattern springs mainly from the plot: as incidents accrete and the plot acquires beauty, the pattern (the book's shape) becomes visible and sustains the aesthetic unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing plot, consider how its sequence and symmetry can generate a satisfying whole. Pattern remains visible after plot details blur; plan modulation and pre-arranged effects if aiming for strong pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sacrifices required for pattern (pruning characters and attributes)
rubrics_metrics.description: To achieve a dominant pattern an author may have to prune: use a short list of characters, limit characters' attributes and sensations, avoid excessive social detail, and remove distractions that would break the pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Henry James's sacrifice for pattern: few characters, 'stingy' construction, exclusion of fun, carnality, or broad social explanation. This curtailment can produce strong unity but risks alienating readers who want fuller life; be aware of the trade-off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-arranged symmetry and modulation produce lasting aesthetic reward
rubrics_metrics.description: A pattern that is carefully organized—symmetry, reciprocal movements of characters (hour-glass), modulation and reservations—yields an enduring aesthetic effect even when minor plot details are forgotten.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design with long-range symmetry and calibrated revelations; the final effect should feel pre-arranged yet organic. The reader's pleasure can be the reward of this aesthetic duty, though it may require the author to 'prune' other elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not mistake figurative structural metaphors for literal devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Metaphors for pattern (hour-glass, grand chain) are pedagogical aids—the critic or reader 'just has a pleasure without knowing why'—they should not be pressed into literal structural prescriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use geometric or pictorial analogies to explain felt unity, but avoid treating them as strict formulas the novel must mechanically follow. The metaphor is explanatory, not a blueprint.
